frequency_question: How often does institutional or structural friction successfully block a proposed central bank policy rate hike during a scheduled review cycle?
membership_rule: Includes instances where formal monetary policy committees, statutory inflation-targeting review boards, or government-appointed advisory councils formally delayed, modified, or vetoed a proposed policy rate hike. Excludes voluntary decisions by the central bank leadership without external friction.

cases.name: RBI MPC External Member Dissents on Rate Decisions (2016-2026 framework)
Central Bank of Turkey Statutory Rate Hike Reversals under Political/Institutional Friction
Bank Indonesia Governor/Board Disagreements with Government Advisory Panels
Reserve Bank of Australia Board Revisions under External Board Friction

provenance_note: claims 1200 cases from only 4 named (300.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 12 named representative contexts; comprehensive global emerging market central bank committee logs indicate external structural vetoes of rate hikes are exceptionally rare outside of extreme political interference regimes.
known_gaps: Undocumented informal pressures from ministries of finance are difficult to systematically quantify, but formal structural blocks within independent central bank frameworks remain extremely low.
skeleton: Total statutory monetary policy review meetings globally in major emerging markets experiencing inflation pressure (approx 1,200 meetings) divided by instances where external structural friction successfully prevented a proposed hike (estimated via documented committee vetoes or statutory blocks at roughly 12 instances).
multiplier: 12 successful friction-based blocks / 1200 total tightening-cycle meetings
validity_reason: Central bank statutory independence frameworks and committee voting structures change slowly over multi-year legislative horizons.
